RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 35

An all-male panel proves nothing by itself — it's unremarkable in banking risk functions and is consistent with both a fair and an unfair process. Treated as your headline argument, it looks speculative and invites dismissal.

The stronger facts are the credential mismatch (PhD plus nine years in the actual discipline versus a master's and a vague "broad experience of regulatory affairs") and the two-week silence on your request for written reasons. Pursue those first: send a dated follow-up, cite any statutory right to reasons in your jurisdiction, and ask what criteria were scored and how.

Keep the panel composition in your notes as context. It becomes meaningful only if the reasons given turn out to be thin or shifting.
